title: The Language of the coast road
premise: Wren Yarrow, a bridge inspector whose marriage has rusted into silence, is hired to assess the old coast road bridge near a dying fishing village. There he meets Edele Okwuosa, the last fluent speaker of Vessic, a language no one under eighty remembers, who asks him to become her final student before her memory fails entirely. As Wren learns the words for things he never knew how to feel, he uncovers photographs implicating his late father in the village's darkest injustice — the drowning of Edele's brother during a strike decades ago. Torn between loyalty to the dead and love for a woman he cannot save, Wren must choose whether justice means punishment or witness. In the end, with Edele's mind dissolving, he speaks her eulogy in Vessic on the bridge itself, forgives his father aloud, and lets his marriage end honestly so that something truer can begin.
about_author: Edmund Okonkwo is a former civil engineer who spent twelve years inspecting coastal infrastructure before turning to fiction full-time. He writes from a rented cottage above a working harbour, where he collects dying dialects the way other men collect stamps.

chapters.title: Expansion Joints
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. He inspects a failing overpass while narrating his marriage in engineering metaphors; his wife Mara doesn't look up when he comes home. The beat: quiet desolation disguised as competence. A letter arrives offering a contract on the remote Kellwick coast road bridge.

chapters.title: The Road That Ends Twice
chapters.summary: Wren drives the coast road to Kellwick, a village the map barely admits exists. First sight of the old iron bridge and the grey house above it. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: unease mixed with relief at being somewhere no one knows his smile.

chapters.title: A Woman of One Grammar
chapters.summary: Wren meets Edele Okwuosa, ninety-one, sharp as a chisel, who corrects his pronunciation of the village name before he's finished saying it. She announces she needs a student before winter takes her memory. POV: Wren. Beat: reluctant fascination.

chapters.title: First Words
chapters.summary: The first lesson: Vessic has no word for 'alone,' only 'unaccompanied by the sea.' Wren finds himself staying past the agreed hour. Intercut with Mara's brief POV chapter — her own loneliness, her own secrets. Beat: two marriages measured in silence.

chapters.title: Load Ratings
chapters.summary: Wren's professional inspection reveals the bridge is worse than reported — and that someone filed false maintenance records years ago. He begins asking questions the council would rather he didn't. POV: Wren. Beat: the inspector starts being inspected by history.

chapters.title: Photographs in a Biscuit Tin
chapters.summary: Edele shows him old photographs of the 1979 fishermen's strike. Wren freezes: his father, young, in a company coat, standing beside the men who were later ruined. POV: Wren. Beat: vertigo — the stranger in the picture is family.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Edele tells the story of her brother Tomas, drowned during the strike when the company locked the safety gates — a story the official record calls an accident. She does not yet know whose son sits in her kitchen. POV: Edele, first time. Beat: grief delivered as testimony.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Wren returns home between contracts; Mara sees through him for the first time in years. They fight about nothing, which means everything. POV alternates Wren/Mara. Beat: the marriage's load rating finally published.

chapters.title: Vocabulary of Guilt
chapters.summary: Back in Kellwick, Wren secretly researches his father's role, finding a signed order in the county archive. He says nothing to Edele but keeps coming to lessons. POV: Wren. Beat: love and deception growing from the same root.

chapters.title: The Word for Forgive
chapters.summary: Edele teaches him that Vessic's word for forgiveness literally means 'to carry together.' She asks him, hypothetically, whether a son owes a father's debts. He lies badly. POV: Wren. Beat: the question becomes a trap he built himself.

chapters.title: Council of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: The parish council pressures Wren to sign off on the bridge as sound — demolition and a cheap replacement serve a developer. His integrity now costs him the contract. POV: Wren. Beat: justice outside the law begins with refusing a signature.

chapters.title: Mara's Chapter
chapters.summary: Mara's POV throughout: she follows Wren's route to Kellwick unannounced, intending confrontation, and instead watches through a window as he laughs — really laughs — with an old woman. Beat: jealousy transmuting into grief for what they both let die.

chapters.title: Edele Forgets a Tuesday
chapters.summary: The first real lapse: Edele calls Wren by her brother's name and sets two cups out of habit. The lessons acquire urgency; he begins recording everything. POV: Wren. Beat: time revealed as the true antagonist.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Water
chapters.summary: On the mudflats below the bridge, Wren tells Edele who he is. Her reaction is not rage but a terrible stillness, then: 'Then you will learn faster.' POV: alternating. Beat: betrayal converted into covenant.

chapters.title: The Locked Gate
chapters.summary: Wren finds the physical gate mechanism from 1979 still rusted shut inside the bridge's service walkway — evidence the lock was manual, deliberate. He documents it. POV: Wren. Beat: proof assembled like a prayer.

chapters.title: Developer's Men
chapters.summary: Intimidation arrives: threats, a vandalized car, an offer of money to lose his report. Villagers split between fear and hope. POV: Wren with a short Edele passage. Beat: rising external pressure as internal stakes peak.

chapters.title: Winter Takes Its First Word
chapters.summary: Edele loses 'harbour' — a word she taught him in week one. She begins dictating the language's last grammar to Wren directly, knowing the recordings may outlive her clarity. POV: Edele. Beat: mortality made grammatical.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Public inquiry into the bridge. Wren presents his findings and the gate evidence; the developer's lawyer attacks his objectivity by exposing his father's name. Mara appears, unexpectedly, to corroborate the archive documents. POV: Wren. Beat: climax of the justice thread — truth spoken at cost.

chapters.title: Carry Together
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the bridge is saved pending restoration; the developer withdraws. But Edele has stopped recognizing Wren except during the lessons, which she clings to like a rail. POV: Wren. Beat: victory shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: The Last Fluent Speaker
chapters.summary: Edele's final lucid evening: she and Wren speak only Vessic, about Tomas, about her father, about whether a language dies if one person carries it. She gives him her brother's notebook. POV: Edele. Beat: transmission completed; farewell begun.

chapters.title: Eulogy on the Bridge
chapters.summary: Edele dies at first frost. At her funeral on the bridge deck, Wren delivers the eulogy half in English, half in Vessic — the language's last public sentence. The village answers with the call-and-response she taught them. POV: Wren. Beat: catharsis; witness as inheritance.

chapters.title: Unaccompanied by the Sea
chapters.summary: Spring. Wren and Mara divorce gently, without villains. He stays in Kellwick teaching six children their great-grandmother's words, and inspects bridges along the coast road, speaking to the sea in a language almost no one else can hear. POV: Wren. Beat: quiet resurrection — identity rebuilt from borrowed words.
